label: prf:quantum-dilog-convergence
title: Proof of quantum dilog convergence
html:
Proof. Proof of quantum dilog convergence

Proof. Each factor is non-zero on the domain: \lvert q^{-k} z\rvert < q^{-k} \cdot q = q^{\,1-k} \leq 1 for k \geq 1, so 1 - q^{-k} z \neq 0 (quantum dilogarithm). Writing a_k = q^{-k} z, the geometric series \sum_{k \geq 1} \lvert a_k\rvert = \lvert z\rvert \sum_{k\geq 1} q^{-k} converges since q > 1. On the domain every denominator obeys the uniform lower bound 1 - a_k \geq 1 - \lvert z\rvert / q > 0, so the deviation terms g_k = (1 - a_k)^{-1} - 1 = a_k/(1 - a_k) satisfy \lvert g_k\rvert \leq \lvert a_k\rvert /(1 - \lvert z\rvert/q) and are summable by comparison. Multipliability of \prod_k (1 + g_k) = \prod_k (1 - a_k)^{-1} then follows from the one-plus-summable criterion for infinite products. \square

This is the convergence half of the brane-tower programme — the claim of brane tower in z-Habiro that survives the refutation of the level-selection rule n_\star. It establishes that \Phi_q is a genuine analytic object on \lvert z\rvert < q, so the z-Habiro Cauchy-limit construction has a well-defined target.

Note (scope). Convergence does not make the per-generator \Phi_q(\lvert\hat V_i\rvert) form a production mass input. At the physical brane-tower argument z_i = \lvert\hat V_i^{\mathrm{full}}\rvert \in [0.85, 1) the product is convergent but enormous (\Phi_q(0.989) \approx 6.7 \times 10^5), which is why the canonical mass tower mass-endomorphism tower evaluates the bounded symmetric form -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-\lvert\hat V_i\rvert) rather than \Phi_q. The proposition closes the analytic existence question, not the regularization question.
